title: The design resubmit is unstaffable: a goal with a design is never offered design.submit again, so version 2 has no producer
definitionOfDone: REPRODUCED FIRST, AGAINST A REAL STORE: a goal with an APPROVED Gate 1 and a design at version 1 is offered `planning.submit_decomposition` and NO `design.submit`. Record `readDesignRevision` answering ok:true at version 1, and record `versionOf(ledger, designAggregateId(goalId))` as a NUMBER. Plus the control: the same goal with no design still offers design.submit and refuses DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT - the row's original premise falsified in delivered bytes.

AFTER THE FIX that goal IS offered `design.submit`, through the production surface against a real store, no stub. The offer's `expectedVersion` is 1, not 0 - asserted. A 0 there ships an offer the store refuses on every attempt, and the ABSENT case cannot detect it because 0 is correct there.

THE RESUBMIT IS NOT STAFFED. The PRESENT arm yields the design.submit OFFER and a `compilerSteps` array containing ONLY the decomposition - both asserted in the same arm. affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1205 and :1215 stay green; a red there means the exclusion is broken.

SKIPPED IS NEVER UNDONE. A goal carrying the skip marker reads SKIPPED against a real store, is offered the decomposition, and gets NO design.submit anywhere in the answer. Old DoD 5 and rail 2, unchanged.

UNREADABLE IS STILL NOT ABSENCE. An unreadable design ledger records its refusal and makes the surface answer REFUSED - asserting the specific code AND the layer that refused, not merely "not ok". Old DoD 3, unchanged.

MUTATION DRILL, TWO ARMS, each quoted with its failing line: (a) revert the PRESENT arm to decomposition-only and DoD 2 goes RED; (b) delete the staffing exclusion and DoD 3 goes RED. Restore per the shared-tree rule - `git status --porcelain` first, back every path up OUT OF TREE, restore FROM THE BACKUP (never `git checkout --`), prove by SHA256 in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

Gates: RECORDED verification is the scoped owned command actually run at exit 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line and every filter/env flag INSIDE the recorded string. Repo-wide `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` are DISCLOSED with exit codes, failing-file sets and the `(AFTER - BEFORE) ∩ owned = ∅` computation. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.
taskRails: MEASURE THE REAL REFUSAL CODE BEFORE FIXING. The description names DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE as the likely answer; reproduce it against a real store and fix what actually fires. A fix aimed at a guessed code ships the defect behind a green test.

UNREADABLE IS NOT ABSENCE - the original principle stands and must survive. A store error or malformed record must never produce a design offer. This row separates 'never designed' from 'cannot be read'; it does not merge them.
NO STUB MAY STAND IN FOR THE THING UNDER TEST. The production `designState` must be exercised against a real store. A stub that agrees with a broken implementation is how this shipped green.
DO NOT CHANGE THE LADDER'S FOUR-STATE SEMANTICS. ABSENT offers the design step; PRESENT and SKIPPED offer the decomposition. This row fixes what produces those states, not what they mean.
NO UI, NO JOURNEY. The card and the browser journey belong to task-33ceae56 and task-f3409f9a.

implementationPlan.description:
**REPRODUCE THE REAL CAUSE ON A REAL STORE. NO PRODUCTION EDITS.** This row was mis-diagnosed twice; the delivered record must carry the measurement, not the story.

Build, against a real SqliteEventStore (the harness `affordance-read-planning.test.ts` already uses), a goal with an APPROVED Gate 1 and a design ALREADY SUBMITTED at version 1 (`submitDesignRevision`, imported at that file's :24). Read the production affordance surface for it and record, quoted:

(a) the `nextAllowedCommands` entries for that goal — expect `planning.submit_decomposition@<goalId>` present and NO `design.submit@design:<goalId>`. This is the defect.
(b) `readDesignRevision(store, {goalRef, projectId})` for that goal answers `ok: true` at version 1 — proving the state is PRESENT, not a refusal. This is what retires the whole 'wrong refusal code' family the previous plan chased.
(c) `versionOf(ledger, designAggregateId(goalId))` for that same goal. Record the NUMBER. It must be 1. If it is 0, STOP and report — the resubmit offer would ship permanently conflicting and the fix changes shape.
(d) THE CONTROL, so the record shows what is NOT broken: the same harness with NO design submitted still offers `design.submit@design:<goalId>` and `readDesignRevision` refuses `DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT`. The row's original premise is falsified in the delivered bytes, not just in a comment.

Record all four in the step note. No file is modified by this step.

implementationPlan.description:

Resolve `input.designState(goal.goalId)` ONCE into a local, then branch on all three states explicitly:

- `"ABSENT"` → `[design.submit @ designAggregateId(goalId)]`. UNCHANGED.
- `"PRESENT"` → `[design.submit @ designAggregateId(goalId), planning.submit_decomposition @ goalId]`. **NEW.** The design exists and the operator may revise it; the decomposition stays offered because the goal is also ready to compile.
- `"SKIPPED"` → `[planning.submit_decomposition @ goalId]`. UNCHANGED, and this is load-bearing: a goal that deliberately skipped its design is NEVER offered one again (row rail 2). Do not collapse SKIPPED into the PRESENT arm.

The four-state MEANINGS are untouched — ABSENT still offers the design step, PRESENT and SKIPPED still offer the decomposition. What changes is that PRESENT now ALSO offers the revision. Write that reason in a comment at the branch; the next reader will otherwise re-derive it wrong, as this row twice proves.

Do not touch `COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS` or `COMPILER_SCHEMA_KINDS`. `design.submit` is already in the first and correctly absent from the second (it does not use the compiler wire).

implementationPlan.description:
**THE FIX, PART 2 — THE RESUBMIT IS AN OPERATOR AFFORDANCE, NOT AGENT WORK.** Same file. Without this, part 1 ships an infinite loop.

MEASURED: `resolvePlanningOffers` at :265-267 pushes every minted offer whose kind is in `COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS` into `compilerSteps`, and `affordance-read.ts:403-410` turns each into a READY staffable step the wrapper picks up. Leaving part 1 alone would staff a design agent onto every already-designed goal on every poll, forever.

Change `offersForGoal`'s return type to carry both sets — `{ readonly offers: readonly NextAllowedCommand[]; readonly staffable: readonly NextAllowedCommand[] }` — and update all six return sites (:175 `[]`, :179, :181, :184-186, :188, :238). For every site EXCEPT the new PRESENT arm, `staffable` is the same array as `offers`. For the PRESENT arm, `staffable` holds ONLY the decomposition: the resubmit is offered to the operator and never staffed.

Then at :263-268 iterate `offers` to fill the offers list and `staffable` to fill `compilerSteps`, so the `COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS.find` filter runs over the staffable set instead of every minted offer.

The file is already 276 lines and this adds roughly 15. That is over the 250 target and well under the 400 split line — do NOT split the file for this row.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — THE RESUBMIT IS OFFERED, NEVER STAFFED. Same file, no other production file touched.

SHAPE: `offersForGoal` now returns `GoalOffers { readonly offers; readonly staffable }` instead of a bare array. Rather than repeat an object literal at every exit, one helper carries the default — `staffAll(offers) => Object.freeze({ offers, staffable: offers })` — so the divergence is visible in exactly one place instead of being spread across ten sites where a future reader could not tell which ones matter.

ALL TEN RETURN SITES CONVERTED (the plan named six; the function has ten, and I audited by `grep -n "return "` over the whole function rather than trusting the count): WITHHELD `staffAll([])`; ABSENT; PRESENT (the divergent one); SKIPPED fall-through; the pendingRevision ternary; `plan.propose`; the DRAFT approval pair; the closeReadiness ternary; COMPLETED; and the final `staffAll([])`. Nine are `staffAll`. One is not:

THE PRESENT ARM, the only divergence:
```ts
const decomposition = offer(input, "planning.submit_decomposition", goal.goalId);
return Object.freeze({
  offers: Object.freeze([offer(input, "design.submit", designAggregateId(goal.goalId)), decomposition]),
  staffable: Object.freeze([decomposition]),
});
```
The decomposition offer is minted ONCE and referenced from both arrays, so the offered command and the staffed step can never be two different mints with two different commandIds.

CONSUMER: `resolvePlanningOffers` now resolves once into `const resolved`, pushes `resolved.offers` into the offers list, and runs the `COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS.find` filter over `resolved.staffable` only. A comment at the loop names what the old shape did — the filter ran over every minted offer, which is precisely what would have staffed the resubmit forever.

TYPECHECK: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 0, non-vacuous (`$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echoed). File 293 -> 322 lines; over the 250 target, under the 400 split line, NOT split (plan risk 2).

THE FIX IS PROVEN BY WHAT DID *NOT* GO RED. Running both owned daemon test files now: `Test Files 2 failed (2)` / `Tests 6 failed | 67 passed (73)` EXIT 1. Every one of the six is a PRESENT-state OFFER-SET assertion — the shape consumers steps 4 and 5 update:

  affordance-planning-offers.test.ts > "offers the dispatcher once Gate 1 is approved and a design exists"
  affordance-planning-offers.test.ts > "offers the compiler for the goal while the successor is created but not yet proposed"
  affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1204 > "offers the exact design work-item only between Gate 1 and the first design"
  affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1249 > "reads the latest revision when skipped=true changes between polls"
  affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1249 > "reads the latest revision when skipped=false changes between polls"
All six fail identically: `expected Set{ 'design.submit', 'planning.submit_decomposition' } to deeply equal Set{ 'planning.submit_decomposition' }` — the resubmit appearing, which is the feature.

CRITICALLY, THE STAFFING ASSERTIONS STAYED GREEN. `affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1205` and `:1215` assert `steps.filter(kind === "design.submit")` is `[]` for the non-ABSENT cases, and NEITHER is in the failing set. Per plan risk 3 and step 5(D), a red there would have meant the staffing exclusion is broken; they are green, so the resubmit is offered and not staffed — measured, not asserted by construction. The same holds for the `compilerSteps` exact-array assertions in the ladder file: the three reds there are all on offer sets, none on `compilerSteps`.

NOTE ON THE skipped=true ARM: it reds too, which looks wrong until you read the loop — that `it.each` writes BOTH a skip and a non-skip revision in sequence, so the iteration where the design is a real revision is PRESENT and correctly gains the offer. SKIPPED itself is unaffected; step 5(B) pins that separately against a real store.

implementationPlan.description:

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 — THE LADDER ARMS, EXACT ARRAYS, ALL THREE STATES. `affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` only. Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 40 passed (40)` EXIT 0 via `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts`. Count is 40 before and after — I replaced a 4-case `it.each` with 4 named arms, so no test was lost or silently added.

THE OLD ARM COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS. It was `it.each([...])("design rung: approved=%s, state=%s offers only %s")` asserting `new Set(offers.map(commandKind))` against `new Set([kind])`. Two weaknesses, both now closed: a Set of KINDS cannot tell a design offer fenced on `design:<goalId>` from one fenced on the goal (the non-dispatchable shape this ladder shipped once before, per the landed `design-offer-fence-is-not-goal-version` finding), and none of the four cases asserted `compilerSteps` at all — so the staffing question was simply not asked. Replaced with a shared `offered(resolution)` helper mapping each offer to `kind@targetAggregateId` IN ORDER, and four named arms:

(a) approved=false: loops all three design states and asserts each offers exactly `[product_contract.propose_revision@<goalId>]` — the design state must not leak into the pre-Gate-1 rung, which the old single-row case never checked.
(b) ABSENT: offers exactly `[design.submit@design:<goalId>]`, compilerSteps exactly `[{design:<goalId>, design.submit}]`. Unchanged behaviour, now pinned on the aggregate too.
(c) PRESENT — THE ROW'S ARM, and both halves live in ONE `it` as the step required: offers exactly `[design.submit@design:<goalId>, planning.submit_decomposition@<goalId>]` AND compilerSteps exactly `[{<goalId>, planning.submit_decomposition}]`. A comment says why they may not be split: an offered-and-staffed resubmit is the infinite design loop, an unoffered-and-unstaffed one is this row's defect, and two separate arms let one rot green while the other passes.
(d) SKIPPED: offers exactly `[planning.submit_decomposition@<goalId>]` and the same single compilerStep. NO `design.submit` anywhere in the answer (row rail 2).

TWO SHAPE CONSUMERS UPDATED, BOTH DEFAULT-PRESENT, NEITHER A STAFFING CHANGE:
- "offers the dispatcher once Gate 1 is approved and a design exists" (was :514) — retitled "...AND the resubmit...", now asserts both offers by `kind@target` via the same `offered` helper instead of kind-only + a separate `offers[0]?.targetAggregateId` probe. - "offers the compiler for the goal while the successor is created but not yet proposed" (was :618) — `resolutionOver` leaves `designState` at its `() => "PRESENT"` default, so the resubmit rides along; the `roster` helper SORTS, so `design.submit` lands first. Comment added naming both facts. Its `compilerSteps` assertion is UNCHANGED and still passes.

THE `[]` ASSERTIONS ARE UNTOUCHED AND GREEN, which is the load-bearing part. All eleven `compilerSteps).toEqual` sites re-read; the four asserting `[]` (:189, :507, :530, :650) were not edited and pass. implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 — THE PRODUCTION-COMPOSITION ARMS, REAL STORE, NO STUB. `affordance-read-planning.test.ts` only. Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 34 passed (34)` EXIT 0 via `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read-planning.test.ts`. 33 -> 34: exactly one arm added, none removed. Every arm here runs the REAL `designState` (`affordance-read.ts:356-365`) through `createAffordancePort` over a real `SqliteEventStore` — no `designState` stub anywhere in the file, which is row rail 3.

(A) THE CAPABILITY IS REACHABLE — new arm, "offers a resubmit fenced on the design head, and the fence tracks TWO resubmits". Approved Gate 1 + a design at v1, then a LOOP over expected `[1, 2]`. Each pass asserts:
  - the surface offers `design.submit` with `expectedVersion: <expected>` AND `targetAggregateId: design:goal-1` (matchObject on both — the aggregate matters as much as the number: a goal-fenced offer would carry a plausible integer and still be dispatch-refused);
  - `steps.filter(kind === "design.submit")` is `[]` — offered, never staffed;
  - `writeDesign(store, ref, designRevisionFixture(), resubmit.expectedVersion).record.version` is `expected + 1` — the offer the SURFACE minted is the one the STORE accepts, dispatched at its own fence rather than at a number the test chose.
I went beyond the step's single-resubmit requirement deliberately, because step 7(d) asks it directly: after the FIRST resubmit lands at v2, the next poll's offer carries `expectedVersion: 2`. A fence that were pinned rather than derived would pass at 1 and fail at 2; this loop is the only thing in the row that distinguishes them.

(B) THE SKIP IS NOT UNDONE — covered twice, both on the real store. The existing "skips the design while the real chain still compiles and reaches approval" arm asserts set-equality `{planning.submit_decomposition}` with no `design.submit`, and passes UNCHANGED. And the `it.each([true, false])` polling arm now DISCRIMINATES the two states inside one journey: `skipped=true` expects `{planning.submit_decomposition}`, `skipped=false` expects `{design.submit, planning.submit_decomposition}`, plus a new assertion that NEITHER state staffs a design step. Before this row that arm asserted the same set for both values, so it could not have seen a SKIPPED regression at all — it is now a real discriminator rather than a shape it happened to share.

(C) UNREADABLE IS STILL NOT ABSENCE — and now, importantly, not PRESENT either. The two existing arms (blindChainStore -> `DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`@`LEDGER`; payload-corrupting Proxy -> `DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED`@`LEDGER`) keep asserting their specific code AND layer, and each gained `expect("nextAllowedCommands" in refused).toBe(false)` and `expect("steps" in refused).toBe(false)`. That is the clause the resubmit made newly load-bearing: `designState` returns `"PRESENT"` on an unreadable read as its fail-closed default, and PRESENT now MINTS A DESIGN OFFER. The only thing preventing a resubmit being offered over a ledger nobody could read is the `designFailures[0]` discard at affordance-read.ts:386. These assertions pin that discard directly instead of inferring it.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE ROW'S PREMISE IS FALSIFIED FOR THE SECOND TIME, AND I FOUND THE REAL CAUSE. Owner ruled the reading on 2026-09-06 (AskUserQuestion, 'Real gap: ladder never offers a resubmit'). Everything below is measured at HEAD moe/work-2026-09-04.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN (do not fix it): a never-designed goal reads ABSENT and IS offered design.submit. worker-deb4c7d8 measured readEvents('design:goal-never') -> [] (does NOT throw), design-store.ts:204 fires DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT, affordance-read.ts:359 maps it to ABSENT, and the ladder offers design.submit. The e2e spec's step 6 (design-operator.spec.ts:320, submitDesign v1) SUCCEEDS on exactly this path, and affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1190 already asserts it green. DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE is not reached. The row's title, description and DoD 1-6 as written all aim at this non-defect.

MY OWN DEDUCTION, INDEPENDENT OF THE WORKER, FROM PRODUCTION SOURCE: affordance-read.ts:386 is `if (designFailures[0] !== undefined) return designFailures[0];` and it runs AFTER resolvePlanningOffers. So a surface answer that CONTAINS offers proves designFailures was empty, which proves the `designFailures.push` branch at :361-365 never ran, which proves `read.ok === true` -- a design record was READABLE. The whole unreadable/refusal-code family is eliminated by the symptom itself.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY FAILS: tests/e2e/control-room/design-operator.spec.ts:340 -- `await submitDesign(ENTITY_V2, "ConfirmDialog", "v2")`, under the comment '8. A resubmit bumps the version and the tab shows the NEWER one (DoD 3)'. That is a RESUBMIT to a goal that already carries Version 1. submitDesign calls offerFor('design.submit') at :302; offerFor fails at :98 with `expect(found, `no ${commandKind} offer among ${seen}`).toBeDefined()`, whose message is literally 'no design.submit offer among ..., planning.submit_decomposition@goal-...' -- the reported symptom verbatim. Then offerFor returns null and submitDesign's `if (offer === null) return;` at :303 returns silently, so execution continues and the visible failure lands four steps later at the card assertion. The spec's own comment at :257 already names that lag as what mis-diagnosed this the first time.

THE REAL GAP: affordance-planning-offers.ts:176-182. `if (designState === "ABSENT") -> design.submit; else -> planning.submit_decomposition`. PRESENT never offers design.submit again. But design.submit IS a versioned revision command (design-contracts.ts:174 designRevisionEventId(goalId, version); design-store.ts:209 selects a wanted version; POST /design/read takes {goalRef, version}) and the shipped UI renders cr.design.version 'Version 2' and 'Design version 2' in the approve fold. Nothing in production can produce version 2. Same defect class as the row's title -- a shipped capability with no operator route -- one version later.

EXPECTED-VERSION RISK, MEASURED AND RETIRED: offer() at :150-159 sets expectedVersion: versionOf(input.ledger, aggregateId), and for design.submit the aggregateId is designAggregateId(goalId) = 'design:<goalId>'. readDurableLedger (bootstrap-ledger.ts:97-112) folds EVERY EFFECTS_COMMITTED decision for the project keyed by targetAggregateId, regardless of family, so a committed design.submit decision IS in the ledger and versionOf returns its real currentVersion. The current code works for ABSENT only because the correct answer there is 0; step 4 must ASSERT the resubmit offer carries 1 after v1, because a ledger that omitted design aggregates would ship a permanently-conflicting offer and look identical at ABSENT.

THE STAFFING HAZARD -- the reason the fix is two-part, not one line. resolvePlanningOffers:265-267 pushes EVERY minted offer whose kind is in COMPILER_OFFER_KINDS (:17-19, which contains design.submit) into compilerSteps, and affordance-read.ts:403-410 turns each compilerStep into a READY staffable step the WRAPPER picks up. Offering the resubmit without excluding it from compilerSteps staffs a design agent onto every already-designed goal on every poll, forever -- an infinite resubmit loop. The resubmit is an OPERATOR affordance, not agent work.
